result.topic_en: Euler finishes describing the boundary conditions for the end of an elastic rod (the simply fixed case with y=0 and d²y/ds²=0, and the 'infixed' clamped case with y=0 and dy/ds=0), notes that the two ends together give four conditions determining the constants and the frequency, and begins Scholion 2 listing the six combinations of end conditions.

III. Tertius cafus efto, quo terminus virgae E ita

Cum igitur hi finguli cafus binas determinationes

tur, fed infuper aequatio refultabit, ex qua ipfam quanti-

items.english: In this case it is clear that, setting s=0, not only must y=0 but also dy/ds=0, because at this end the tangent must coincide with the axis itself.

items.english: Four conditions will always arise, by which not only the constants α, β, γ, δ are determined, but moreover an equation will result from which the quantity f, and hence the simple pendulum k, can be assigned.
